newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cemig auction to draw just one bid-paper.
newsitem.headline: Cemig auction to draw just one bid-paper.

text.p: The auction of debentures representing a 32-percent voting stake in Brazilian power firm Cemig will draw just one bid although five groups are pre-qualified for the tender, a local newspaper said.

Financial daily Gazeta Mercantil, quoting federal National Development Bank (BNDES) Vice President Jose Pio Borges, said only a group made up of U.S.-based AES Corp and Southern Electric and a fund created by local bank Opportunity plans to present an offer.
BNDESPar, the investment arm of BNDES, has set a base price of 1.13 billion reais or 60.37 reais per 1,000 shares for debentures convertible to Cemig common stock.
The auction, intended to gain a strategic partner for the firm, is slated for 0900 local/1200 gmt on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange.
Borges was quoted as saying other groups have decided not to bid because of the tough requirements set forth in the bid specifications for the sale.
"Pacific Corporation, one of the pre-qualified firms, desisted from the auction because it wanted more time to analyze the deal," he was quoted as saying.
Minas Gerais state, however, wants to press ahead with the long-delayed auction in order to avoid further legal challenges that could scuttle the sale.
Borges also was quoted as saying the base price also appears to have scarred off other potential bidders.

The voting stake in Cemig was originally slated to be auctioned late last year but was repeatedly delayed. On Tuesday, Cemig officials said they had knocked down all court injunctions aimed at scuttling the sale.
